theater: 長安、洛陽兩京及澧水河陽一線

battle.name: 唐收復兩京之戰
battle.theater: 長安、洛陽兩京及澧水河陽一線
battle.brief: 至德二載（757）九月，廣平王李俶掛帥、郭子儀副帥，率朔方等軍及回紇精騎十五萬自鳳翔西進，於長安城西香積寺北大破偽燕十萬眾，斬首六萬級，繼而入西京、東指收復洛陽。卡面的羅馬標槍未入華土，其投槍破盾的戰法在本役由唐軍標槍與弓弩分擔，破陣主力是李嗣業陌刀如牆而進的前軍。

kit.name: 羅馬標槍
kit.history: 半米長的投槍，槍桿中空。捅穿盾之後就折斷，敵人只能帶著半截槍退回掩體。

countries: 至德二載（757）秋，收復兩京的作戰在唐廷與安史偽燕兩套軍事體系之間展開。唐軍一方名義上是聯軍，實際上號令歸一：元帥廣平王李俶掛名統軍，副元帥郭子儀行軍總制，作戰序列分為前軍、中軍、後軍，前軍由鎮西、北庭行營節度使李嗣業領，中軍郭子儀自將，後軍王思禮；兵源為朔方、河東、河中、北庭、劍南、隴右、關中京畿宿衛以及招安後的雜部，另有回紇精騎四千餘人與西域諸國部眾隨軍聽用，監軍內侍與判元帥府行軍司馬坐鎮幕府，替朝廷直接駕馭外軍。燕軍一方以安慶緒為帝，嚴莊掌機要，兵分數路：安守忠屯西京，崔乾祐守洛陽與華州，李歸仁為前鋒，張通儒、田乾真等分守城門；骨幹是范陽、平盧、成德三鎮帶來的契丹、同羅、奚、室韋騎兵，關中則靠徵發的市卒、降戶與兩京強編的雜兵湊數，攻城備有雲梯、撞車與擲石。兩套體系的分野很清楚：唐軍靠節度使分道與元帥幕府統一，回紇盟軍自成一軍、賞賜另計；燕軍各節度使擁兵自重，河北與關中彼此脫節，一旦失掉洛陽與長安，中樞便無所依憑。
countriesEn: The campaign that retook the two capitals in the autumn of 757 was fought between two military systems: a Tang coalition reassembled in the northwest, and the Yan state the rebels had built in the two capitals. On the Tang side the force was nominally a coalition but functioned under a single hand. The Prince of Guangping, Li Chu, was named supreme commander, Guo Ziyi served as deputy commander and conducted the march, and the order of battle was split into a vanguard under Li Siye, who held the commands of Zhenxi and Beiting, a central army led by Guo Ziyi in person, and a rear guard under Wang Sili. The troops were drawn from the Shuofang, Hedong, Hezhong, Beiting, Jiannan, Longyou and capital-region garrisons, together with surrendered and recruited formations, more than four thousand Uighur horsemen and contingents from the Western Regions. Court eunuchs acting as supervisors and a commissioner of military affairs sat in the headquarters so that the throne could steer the field armies directly. On the Yan side the emperor was An Qingxu, with Yan Zhuo holding civil affairs, and the command was scattered across several posts: An Shouzhong garrisoned the western capital, Cui Qianyou held Luoyang and Huazhou, Li Guiren led the vanguard, and Zhang Tongru, Tian Qianzhen and others took charge of the gates. The backbone of the Yan army was the Khitan, Tongluo, Xi and Shiwei cavalry carried up from the Fanyang, Pinglu and Chengde circuits of Hebei, supplemented in Guanzhong by pressed town militia, surrendered households and mixed levies drafted from the two capitals, with scaling ladders, battering rams and stone-throwers for siege work. The difference in method is plain: the Tang army obeyed one chain of command running from the circuit commanders up to the headquarters, while the Uighur contingent kept its own organisation and was paid separately; the Yan circuits each held their own men and were poorly joined to one another, so that once Luoyang and Chang'an were lost the rebel centre had nothing left to stand on.
people: 關鍵人物分屬兩側。唐廷一方，元帥廣平王李俶是肅宗李亨的長子，時年尚幼，掛名統軍而實權在副元帥郭子儀手中；他在兩京易主之日顯出分寸：回紇葉護依約要取金帛子女時，他拜於馬前力諫，說若遽然掠奪，東京之人必皆固守而不可復取，葉護乃跪捧其足答應直趨東京。郭子儀在扶風留宴回紇三日，途中設法穩住盟軍，返京後又奉命經略河北；僕固懷恩為朔方左廂兵馬使，引回紇擊潰敵伏於陣東的精騎，戰後屢請追擊安守忠、李歸仁而未獲准許，本役最大的失誤正出在此處。前軍主將李嗣業以陌刀破陣最著，兵臨河內又擊退蔡希德、崔乾祐的兩萬步騎，事後卻被監軍魚朝恩進讒，詔令就河中斬之，陌刀前鋒的骨幹自此折損。都知兵馬使王難得在亂軍中救裨將，中箭及眉，血流被面而戰不止。行在一側由肅宗坐鎮鳳翔，遣中使啖庭瑤入蜀奏上皇，命左僕射裴冕入京師告郊廟，李泌則勸上皇東歸。燕軍一方，安慶緒弒父自立後坐鎮鄴城；安守忠在長安失守前已率眾遁走，其後奉安慶緒之命赴范陽徵兵並密謀除史思明，反被史思明扣押，隨竇子昂奉表歸唐；崔乾祐守洛陽，李歸仁引眾挑戰，張通儒、田乾真與安守忠同夜逃散。史思明以所部十三郡及兵八萬降唐，一度讓河北歸唐，安慶緒卻又與史思明交惡，河北的向背自此再無定準。
peopleEn: The decisive figures belong to both sides. On the Tang side the Prince of Guangping, Li Chu, was the eldest son of the Suzong emperor Li Heng and still young; he held the title of commander while real power stayed with the deputy commander Guo Ziyi. In the very hours in which the two capitals changed hands he showed judgement: when the Uighur prince Yehu claimed the gold, silk and women promised by treaty, Li Chu knelt at his horse and argued that if they plundered at once, the people of the eastern capital would all shut themselves in and resist, and Yehu leapt from his horse, took Li Chu's feet in his hands and promised to march straight on Dongdu. Guo Ziyi held the Uighur camp for three days at Fufeng, kept the alliance steady on the march and was later charged with managing Hebei. Pugu Huai'en, commander of the left division of the Shuofang army, brought the Uighur riders against the enemy cavalry hidden on the east of the line and cut them to pieces, and afterwards asked again and again to pursue An Shouzhong and Li Guiren, only to be refused; the gravest error of the campaign began at that refusal. Li Siye, commander of the vanguard, was most famous for breaking the enemy with the modao blade, and he later repelled Cai Xide and Cui Qianyou with twenty thousand foot and horse at the mouth of the Yellow River; he was then slandered by the supervisor eunuch Yu Chao'en and put to death by order at Hezhong, and the spine of the modao vanguard was broken with him. Wang Nande, the officer commanding the troops, was wounded in the brow while rescuing one of his own generals, the arrow still hanging, blood running over his face, and he fought on. At the field headquarters the Suzong emperor sat at Fengxiang, sent the palace messenger Yan Tingyao into Shu to report to the retired emperor, ordered the chancellor Pei Mian into the capital to announce to the temples and console the people, and Li Mi advised the retired emperor to come east. On the Yan side An Qingxu, who had killed his father and taken the throne, sat at Ye; An Shouzhong had already slipped away with his men before Chang'an fell and was afterwards sent by An Qingxu to Fanyang to call up troops and plot against Shi Siming, only to be detained by Shi Siming and to surrender with Dou Zi'ang and a memorial; Cui Qianyou held Luoyang, Li Guiren led the challenge, and Zhang Tongru and Tian Qianzhen fled with An Shouzhong in the night. Shi Siming surrendered with the thirteen prefectures and eighty thousand men he commanded, which for a while brought Hebei back to the Tang, yet An Qingxu and Shi Siming remained hostile to each other, and from then on the loyalties of the north had no settled direction.
kits: 卡面那件羅馬標槍，是半米長的投槍：槍桿中空，前段加配重，捅穿盾面之後槍桿即折，敵人只能帶著半截槍退回掩體。它在羅馬軍團手中屬輕裝投射兵器，交手之前用來拆散對方的盾陣與密集隊形，讓重裝步兵得以逼近，本身並不適合近身纏鬥，也從未出現在七五七年的關中戰場。本役裡與它功能相應的，是唐軍步卒的標槍、投槊與弓弩：先以投射兵器在兩軍尚未貼上之前壓制射線，逼燕軍舉盾、收隊，再由陌刀手結陣取隙。長刀是唐軍破陣的骨幹，資治通鑑記李嗣業帥前軍各執長刀如牆而進，當其刀者人馬俱碎；長槊、橫刀、角弓、蹶張弩、方盾與圓盾、明光鎧與札甲，構成步騎合戰的裝備；騎兵用馬槊與彎刀，回紇精騎配複合短弓與輕便馬具，來去如風。攻城器械備有雲梯、巢車、攻城車與擲石機，本役卻未大規模使用，真正的勝負是在野外交鋒中決出的。運輸靠河中蒲州、絳州的糧倉與漕運，車隊芻粟先行於大軍，繒帛則是酬謝回紇的貨幣，也是一場仗裡最直接的一筆物資流向。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card face is the Roman pilum, a throwing spear half a metre long: the shaft is hollow, the forward section is weighted, and once it has punched through a shield the shaft snaps, so that the man on the other end can only withdraw behind his cover carrying half a spear. In Roman hands it was a light missile belonging to the skirmish line, used before contact to break up the enemy's shield wall and close order so that the armoured infantry could close in; it was never a close-combat weapon, and it never appeared on the battlefield of Guanzhong in 757. What filled the same function in this campaign was the Tang foot soldier's throwing spear and javelin together with the bow and the strong crossbow: missiles were used to dominate the field while the two lines were still apart, forcing the Yan troops to raise their shields and tighten their formation, after which the modao men closed in and took the gaps. The long blade was the spine of the Tang assault; the Zizhi Tongjian records that Li Siye led the vanguard with long blades in their hands, advancing like a wall, and those who met the blade were cut apart men and horses together. Long spears, horizontal sabres, horn bows, strong crossbows, square and round shields, Mingguang armour and lamellar harness made up the equipment of the combined foot and horse force; the horsemen carried horse lances and curved sabres, while the Uighur riders used composite short bows and light harness that let them strike and vanish. Ladders, siege towers, siege carriages and stone-throwers were prepared for the attack on the walls, but were never used on any large scale; the real decision of the battle was made in the open field. Supply ran on the granaries and the river transport of Puzhou and Jiangzhou in Hezhong, with wagons of fodder and grain moving ahead of the army, while bolts of silk were the currency in which the Uighur allies were paid, and the most direct flow of goods in the whole campaign.
tactics: 本役的戰術主軸是集結、壓迫與野戰破陣，而非攻城。九月，諸軍集於鳳翔行在，回紇葉護與將軍帝德率精兵四千餘人抵達，郭子儀在扶風留宴三日，日給其軍羊二百口、牛二十頭、米四十斛；庚子諸軍俱發，壬寅至長安城西，陳於香積寺北澧水之東，李嗣業為前軍、郭子儀為中軍、王思禮為後軍，賊眾十萬陳於其北。李歸仁出挑戰，官軍逐之反被乘，軍中驚亂，賊爭趣輜重；李嗣業乃肉袒執長刀立於陣前大呼奮擊，當其刀者人馬俱碎，殺數十人陣乃稍定，遂帥前軍各執長刀如牆而進。敵伏精騎於陣東欲襲官軍之後，僕固懷恩引回紇就擊，翦滅殆盡，李嗣業又與回紇出賊陣後與大軍交擊，自午及酉斬首六萬級，賊遂大潰，餘眾入城，迨夜囂聲不止。追擊環節出了岔子：僕固懷恩請以二百騎追縛安守忠、李歸仁，廣平王以將軍疲弊為由不許，遲明諜至，守忠、歸仁與張通儒、田乾真皆已遁矣。盟軍分配亦是一場交鋒：朝廷與回紇約定克城之日土地士庶歸唐、金帛子女皆歸回紇，葉護欲即如約，廣平王拜於其馬前力陳利害，葉護乃答拜、捧足而應。大軍入城後，廣平王留長安鎮撫三日，引大軍東出，以虢王巨為西京留守，隨即轉入洛陽追擊，一路追奔至河陽，安慶緒退保鄴城。佔領之後的處置同樣是戰術的一部分：官軍既克京城，宗廟之器及府庫資財多散在民間，遣使檢括頗有煩擾，朝廷敕令盡停，命京兆尹李峴安撫坊市；對陷賊官員則採六等定罪，斬達奚珣等十八人於城西南獨柳樹下，陳希烈等七人賜自盡。
tacticsEn: The operational pattern of this campaign was concentration, pressure and a set-piece battle in the open field rather than any assault on the city walls. In the ninth month the armies assembled at Fengxiang, where the field headquarters sat, and the Uighur prince Yehu and the general Dide arrived with more than four thousand picked riders; Guo Ziyi kept them feasting for three days at Fufeng, supplying their camp each day with two hundred sheep, twenty oxen and forty hu of rice. On the gengzi day the column set out, and on the renyin day it reached the west of Chang'an, taking position north of the Xiangji Temple east of the Li River, with Li Siye's vanguard in front, Guo Ziyi in the centre and Wang Sili in the rear against the rebel ten thousand drawn up to the north. Li Guiren came out to give challenge; the Tang troops gave chase, were thrown back and thrown into confusion, and the enemy rushed for the baggage. Li Siye then bared his torso, took his long blade, stood in front of the line and roared his charge; men and horses that met the blade were cut apart, several dozen were killed, and the line steadied, after which he led the vanguard forward with long blades in their hands, advancing like a wall. The enemy had hidden picked cavalry on the east of the field to fall on the Tang rear; Pugu Huai'en brought the Uighur against them and cut them almost to nothing, and Li Siye with the Uighur rode out behind the enemy formation and struck together with the main body, from noon to the fifth hour cutting down sixty thousand, filling the ditches with the dead, until the rebel army collapsed and the survivors ran into the city, where the uproar did not stop until night. The pursuit went wrong: Pugu Huai'en asked to take two hundred horsemen after An Shouzhong and Li Guiren to seize them alive, but the Prince of Guangping, citing the weariness of his general, refused; by the next morning the scouts reported that Shouzhong, Guiren, Zhang Tongru and Tian Qianzhen had all escaped. Even the division of the spoils was a contest: the throne had agreed with the Uighur that on the day the city fell the land and the people would revert to the Tang while gold, silk and women would go to the allies, and Yehu wanted to act on that at once, so the Prince of Guangping knelt before his horse and set out the consequences, until Yehu answered the salute, took his feet in his hands and gave his word. After the army entered the city, the Prince of Guangping remained three days at Chang'an to settle it, then led the host east, leaving the Prince of Guo as warden of the western capital; he then turned on Luoyang, pursued the enemy as far as Heyang, and drove An Qingxu back to hold at Ye. The handling of the occupied city was likewise part of the operation: once the city was taken, the ritual vessels of the ancestral temple and the stores of the treasuries lay scattered among the people, and the emissaries sent to collect them caused much harassment, so the court stopped the search and ordered the governor of Jingzhao, Li Xian, to settle the wards and markets. Those who had served the rebels were sorted into six degrees of punishment: eighteen men including Daxi Xun were beheaded at the Daliu tree south-west of the city, and seven others including Chen Xilie were given leave to kill themselves.
data: 可核的數字大致如下。九月丁亥，元帥廣平王李俶將朔方等軍及回紇、西域之眾十五萬、號稱二十萬，自鳳翔出發；回紇方面，懷仁可汗遣其子葉護及將軍帝德率精兵四千餘人來，抵鳳翔後由朝廷按日供應羊二百口、牛二十頭、米四十斛。行軍與戰鬥的時距是：庚子諸軍俱發，壬寅即抵長安城西，癸卯大軍入西京，前後不過數日。燕軍方面，陳於長安城北者眾十萬，前鋒李歸仁出挑戰。戰果記載為自午及酉斬首六萬級，填溝塹死者甚眾，餘眾入城後夜間喧囂不止。追擊未果一節也有明確記載：僕固懷恩請以二百騎追縛安守忠、李歸仁被拒，遲明守忠、歸仁與張通儒、田乾真皆已遁走。同一時期的降附數字可作對照：史思明以所部十三郡及兵八萬降唐，其使竇子昂奉表至京師，史思明封歸義王、任范陽節度使；而燕主安慶緒治下的平原太守王暕、清河太守宇文寬來降後反被蔡希德、安太清攻拔生擒，於鄴市斬首。收復後的處置數目也有存錄：陷賊官員依六等定罪，重者斬於市，達奚珣等十八人斬於城西南獨柳樹下，陳希烈等七人賜自盡。軍制上另置左右神武軍，取元從子弟充，制皆如四軍，總謂北牙六軍；又擇善騎射者千人為殿前射生手，分左右廂，號英武軍。行政上同時升河中防禦使為節度使，領蒲、絳等七州，分劍南為東西川節度使，置荊澧節度使，安西改稱鎮西。須留意數字有虛實之別：安史之亂中曾有十四節度使統兵五十餘萬之說，而潼關一役關中精兵二十萬數日之間全潰，兵額與戰力並不能直接換算；本役真正倚重的是朔方、北庭一系的精兵與回紇的四千餘騎。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. On the dinghai day of the ninth month the supreme commander, the Prince of Guangping, Li Chu, took the armies of Shuofang together with the Uighur and Western Regions contingents, one hundred and fifty thousand men in all, announced as two hundred thousand, and set out from Fengxiang. On the Uighur side the khagan, Huai'en, sent his son Yehu and the general Dide with more than four thousand picked horsemen; once they reached Fengxiang the court fed them daily with two hundred sheep, twenty oxen and forty hu of rice. The time between marching and battle was short: the column set out on the gengzi day, stood before the west of Chang'an on the renyin day, and entered the western capital on the guimao day. On the Yan side ten thousand were drawn up north of the city, with Li Guiren coming out to give challenge. The result is recorded as sixty thousand heads cut off between noon and the fifth hour, with the ditches filled by the dead, and the survivors running into the city, where the noise did not cease through the night. The failure of the pursuit is equally recorded: Pugu Huai'en asked to take two hundred horsemen after An Shouzhong and Li Guiren to take them alive, was refused, and by the following morning Shouzhong, Guiren, Zhang Tongru and Tian Qianzhen had all escaped. The surrenders of the same period give a useful comparison: Shi Siming came over with the thirteen prefectures and eighty thousand men he held, his envoy Dou Zi'ang arriving at the capital with the memorial, and he was made Prince of Guiyi and military governor of Fanyang. On the other side of the ledger, the Yan governors of Pingyuan and Qinghe, Wang Jian and Yuwen Kuan, who offered themselves to the Tang, were attacked and taken by Cai Xide and An Taiqing and beheaded in the market at Ye. The numbers of the settlement after the recapture are also preserved: those who had served the rebels were graded into six degrees, the gravest executed in the marketplace, eighteen men including Daxi Xun beheaded at the Daliu tree south-west of the city, seven including Chen Xilie given leave to kill themselves. On the military side, left and right Divine Warrior Guards were raised from the sons of the original troops, on the model of the four armies and collectively called the six armies of the north teeth; a thousand men skilled at riding and shooting were selected as the mounted sharpshooters of the palace guard, divided into right and left divisions and called the Valiant Warriors. Administratively, the Hezhong defence commissioner was raised to a military governorate holding the seven prefectures of Puzhou and Jiangzhou and others; Jiannan was split into the East and West Sichuan commands, a Jing-Li command was created, and Anxi was renamed Zhenxi. The figures must be read with care: the rebellion is said at one point to have put more than five hundred thousand men under fourteen military governors, yet at Tongguan the twenty thousand picked troops of Guanzhong were destroyed in a few days, so paper strength and fighting strength cannot simply be converted one into the other. What this campaign truly relied on was the hard core of the Shuofang and Beiting armies and the four thousand odd Uighur riders.
cause: 戰爭的根子在安祿山於天寶十四載（755）冬以奉密詔討楊國忠為名在范陽起兵。兩年之間叛軍打下洛陽與潼關，756年入長安，玄宗夜出延秋門入蜀，太子李亨在靈武即位，是為肅宗，改元至德；朝廷在靈州與鳳翔重建，卻只剩朔方等西北邊軍可用。潼關之敗是關鍵：哥舒翰被迫率二十萬弱兵出關，數日之間全軍覆沒，關中精兵盡喪，兩京的府庫兵械為叛軍所掠，關中文吏淪為叛軍所署，唐廷在關中一時空虛。叛軍佔了兩京，卻沒有把河北與關中真正連成一體：范陽、平盧、成德各擁重兵，擁兵自重，河北郡縣多望風歸唐，關中則只餘破城與缺糧的守軍。轉折出在至德二載正月，安慶緒弒父安祿山自立，忌史思明之強，遣阿史那承慶、安守忠赴范陽徵兵並陰謀除之；史思明在判官耿仁智、裨將烏承玼勸說之下，幡然悔悟，囚承慶等而遣竇子昂奉所部十三郡及兵八萬降唐。河北骨幹反正，叛軍的騎兵與精兵頓失一大半，中樞與河北的斷裂再也補不上，朝廷於是乘勢以廣平王李俶為元帥、郭子儀為副元帥，會朔方諸道之兵並借回紇精騎西向收復兩京。促成決戰的還有幾層現實算盤：唐廷需要首都來承接禮儀與漕運、需要名分來號令河北；叛軍則糧道被斷、援軍不至，安守忠等在長安無法久守，而與回紇結盟的代價是金帛與人口，這筆買賣在肅宗看來仍然划算，因為關中比燕地更值得拿回來。
causeEn: The quarrel had its origin in the winter of 755, when An Lushan rose in Fanyang under the pretext of a secret imperial order to punish Yang Guozhong. Within two years the rebels had taken Luoyang and Tongguan, and in 756 they entered Chang'an; the Xuanzong emperor slipped out of the city at night and journeyed to Shu, while the crown prince Li Heng took the throne at Lingwu as the Suzong emperor and changed the era to Zhide. The court rebuilt itself at Lingzhou and Fengxiang, but the only troops it really had were the frontier garrisons of the northwest. The defeat at Tongguan was the hinge of everything: Guo Shuhan was forced to take two hundred thousand poorly trained men out of the pass, and in a few days the entire army was destroyed, the picked troops of Guanzhong were wiped out, the treasuries and armoury of the two capitals were stripped by the rebels, and the civil officers of Guanzhong became the rebels' own appointees. The rebels held the two capitals, yet they never truly joined Hebei to Guanzhong: Fanyang, Pinglu and Chengde each kept their own armies, and the prefectures of Hebei surrendered in droves, while in Guanzhong nothing was left but broken walls and hungry garrisons. The turn came in the first month of Zhide 2. An Qingxu killed his father An Lushan and took the throne, then, fearing the strength of Shi Siming, sent the general Ashina Chengqing and An Shouzhong to Fanyang to call up troops and to plot against him in secret. Persuaded by his adjudicator Geng Renzhi and his officer Wu Chengjie, Shi Siming changed his mind, detained the emissaries and sent Dou Zi'ang to the court with a memorial offering the thirteen prefectures and eighty thousand men under his command. With the backbone of Hebei turning back to the Tang, the rebel cavalry lost more than half its strength and the gap between the rebel centre and the north could no longer be closed. The court moved at once, naming the Prince of Guangping, Li Chu, as supreme commander and Guo Ziyi as deputy, gathering the troops of the Shuofang circuits and borrowing Uighur horse to drive west and retake the two capitals. There were practical calculations behind the decision as well. The Tang needed the capital to carry the rites and the river transport, and needed a lawful title to command the north; the rebels, cut off from their supply line and denied aid, could not hold the city for long, and the price of the Uighur alliance was measured in gold, silk and people, a price the Suzong emperor was willing to pay, because Guanzhong was worth far more to him than the rebel country.
impact: 兩京的收復是安史之亂的轉折點，卻不是終點。政治上，西京與東都重歸唐室，肅宗的政令自此有了腹地與禮儀之所，遣裴冕入京告郊廟、宣慰百姓，改元乾元、大赦天下，又議上皇自蜀東歸，唐室的官署、籍帳與漕運重新接續；玄宗父子先後入城，卻留下難解的猜忌，李泌的勸諫只能保住表面的團圓。清算陷賊官員一事更見出政令的兩面：崔器、呂諲主張一律處死，李峴力爭而從其議，採六等定罪，既誅首惡，又開歸降之路，資治通鑑的史論仍責其寬縱。軍制上另置左右神武軍與英武軍，重建北牙六軍，禁軍與外軍的比重重新調整；制度上則升河中防禦使為節度使，分劍南為東西川，置荊澧節度使，安西改鎮西，節度使的權力與管轄區一齊膨脹，河北三鎮的割據自此有了制度上的源頭，回紇借兵收復失地也開了先例，其代價是僕固懷恩與唐室由合作走向猜忌，終至再起兵端。代價同樣落在人上：前軍主將李嗣業被讒賜死於河中，陌刀突擊的骨幹自此受損；史思明降而復叛，758年再引燕軍入關，兩京兩度易手，唐軍以六十萬眾圍鄴城而不能克，說明收復兩京的勝利並未轉化為河北的勝利。經濟與城市上，兩京殘破，漕運中斷，洛陽一帶荒穢，直到五代只有後唐定都洛陽，北方政治重心的移動已在此時埋下伏線。
impactEn: The recapture of the two capitals was the turning point of the An Lushan rebellion, though not its end. Politically the western and eastern capitals returned to the Tang, and the Suzong emperor's orders now had a hinterland and a place for the rites: Pei Mian was sent into the capital to announce to the ancestral temple and console the people, the era was changed to Qianyuan, a general amnesty was proclaimed, and the return of the retired emperor from Shu was debated, so that the registers, the officials and the river transport of the dynasty could be joined again. The father and son did come back into the city, but the suspicion between them remained, and Li Mi's counsel could preserve nothing more than the appearance of reunion. The punishment of those who had served the rebels shows the two faces of the new government: Cui Qi and Lü Xun argued that all of them should be put to death, Li Xian argued against it and the court followed him in grading the offenders into six degrees, executing the ringleaders while leaving the way open to those who came back, and the commentary in the Zizhi Tongjian still condemns the leniency. On the military side the left and right Divine Warrior Guards and the Valiant Warriors were raised, the six armies of the north teeth were rebuilt, and the balance between the palace guards and the provincial armies was readjusted. On the institutional side the Hezhong defence command was raised to a military governorate, Jiannan was split into East and West Sichuan, a Jing-Li command was created and Anxi was renamed Zhenxi; the power and the territory of the military governors grew together, and the three Hebei circuits that would rule themselves owed their origin to this arrangement. Borrowing Uighur horse to retake lost ground set a precedent too, and its price was that Pugu Huai'en moved from partnership with the Tang to suspicion of it and finally to another rising. The cost fell on men as well: Li Siye was slandered and put to death at Hezhong, and the spine of the modao assault was broken with him; Shi Siming surrendered and rose again, bringing the Yan army back into the passes in 758, and the two capitals changed hands twice more. Sixty thousand men could not close around Ye, which showed that the victory at the two capitals had not been converted into a victory in Hebei. Economically the two capitals lay in ruins and the river transport was broken; the eastern capital's countryside went barren, and the fact that only Later Tang of the Five Dynasties made Dongdu its capital shows that the shift of the northern centre of gravity had already begun.
result: 至德二載九月丁亥，朔方等軍及回紇、西域之眾十五萬發自鳳翔；壬寅至長安城西香積寺北澧水之東，李歸仁出挑戰，官軍先挫，李嗣業肉袒執長刀立陣前，殺數十人乃稍定，前軍各執長刀如牆而進，敵伏於陣東的精騎為僕固懷恩引回紇擊滅，自午至酉斬首六萬級，賊大潰入城。癸卯大軍入西京，府庫、宗廟之器與兩京印信文書重新入唐軍之手。追擊一節，僕固懷恩請以二百騎追縛安守忠、李歸仁，廣平王拒之，遲明守忠、歸仁、張通儒、田乾真皆已遁去；安慶緒聞西京失守，棄洛陽北走保鄴，唐軍乘勝東出，留虢王巨鎮西京，三日而東，收洛陽，追奔至河陽，兩京以數日之功復歸朝廷。回紇依約取金帛女子，經廣平王力諫方止。歸附之師亦在同時收束：史思明以十三郡八萬眾降唐，封歸義王、任范陽節度使，河北郡縣多望風歸唐；然安慶緒與史思明旋即交惡，史思明復叛，758年再圖兩京。勝後的處置是雙面的：陷賊官按六等定罪，軍器府庫因檢括民間財貨而擾民，朝廷敕停搜括，命京兆尹安撫坊市，同時置左右神武軍與英武軍，重建北牙六軍。整體看，唐收復兩京之戰是安史之亂中唐軍成建制奪回首都的一次成功：名分、禮儀與漕運接續由此恢復，叛軍失去中樞與河北的支持。然而它沒有解決戰爭：安守忠、李歸仁等得脫而入史思明陣中，河北再度反覆；李嗣業被讒賜死於河中，突擊骨幹折損；翌年九節度使六十萬眾圍鄴城而為史思明所破，圍解，兩京再失，戰爭又拖了五年，直至763年史朝義自縊才告結束。收復兩京是這場戰爭的名義勝利，藩鎮坐大與外兵干政才是它的實質遺產。
resultEn: On the dinghai day of the ninth month of Zhide 2 the armies of Shuofang with the Uighur and Western Regions contingents, one hundred and fifty thousand men announced as two hundred thousand, set out from Fengxiang. On the renyin day they stood west of Chang'an, north of the Xiangji Temple east of the Li River; Li Guiren gave challenge, the Tang line was thrown back and thrown into confusion, and Li Siye bared his torso, took his long blade and stood in front of the army until a few dozen were killed and the line steadied, then led the vanguard forward with long blades like a wall, while the enemy cavalry hidden on the east of the field was cut up by Pugu Huai'en with the Uighur, and from noon to the fifth hour sixty thousand were cut down and the rebels broke and ran into the city. On the guimao day the army entered the western capital, and the treasuries, the vessels of the ancestral temple and the seals and registers of the two capitals came back into Tang hands. The pursuit failed: Pugu Huai'en asked to take two hundred horsemen after An Shouzhong and Li Guiren to seize them alive, the Prince of Guangping refused, and by the following morning Shouzhong, Guiren, Zhang Tongru and Tian Qianzhen had all escaped. When An Qingxu learned that the western capital was lost he abandoned Luoyang and rode north to hold at Ye; the Tang army turned east, left the Prince of Guo to guard the western capital, and in three days was in the eastern capital, pursuing as far as Heyang, so that the two capitals returned to the court within a few days. The Uighur took the gold, silk and women promised by the treaty, and only the Prince of Guangping's remonstrance stopped them. Submission was gathered at the same time: Shi Siming came over with the thirteen prefectures and eighty thousand men, was made Prince of Guiyi and military governor of Fanyang, and the prefectures of Hebei surrendered in droves; but An Qingxu and Shi Siming soon fell out again, and in 758 Shi Siming rose once more and aimed at the two capitals. The settlement after the victory had two sides. Those who had served the rebels were graded into six degrees of punishment; the search of private houses for the rebels' treasure caused such harassment that the court stopped it and ordered the governor of Jingzhao to settle the wards and markets; and at the same time the left and right Divine Warrior Guards and the Valiant Warriors were raised and the six armies of the north teeth rebuilt. Taken as a whole, the recapture of the two capitals was the one occasion in the An Lushan rebellion when the Tang army took a capital back in formed order: legitimacy, ritual and the river transport were restored with it, and the rebels lost their centre and the support of the north. Yet it settled nothing. An Shouzhong, Li Guiren and the others escaped and ended up in Shi Siming's ranks, and Hebei began to turn again; Li Siye was slandered and put to death at Hezhong, and the spine of the assault was broken; the next year nine military governors with six hundred thousand men were beaten by Shi Siming at Ye, the siege was lifted, and the two capitals were lost again, so that the war dragged on for another five years until Shi Chaoyi hanged himself in 763. Retaking the two capitals was the nominal victory of the war; the fiefding of the provincial governors and the intervention of foreign cavalry were its real inheritance.
